sources.entry: Homarr - Sleek, modern dashboard with many integrations and web-based config. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Nodejs
Homarr | Sleek server dashboard with drag-and-drop widgets and integrations

summary.one_liner: Homarr is a self-hosted, web-based dashboard with drag-and-drop widgets and integrations for many self-hosted apps.
summary.what_it_does: Homarr provides a customizable dashboard built on a drag-and-drop grid, where apps and widgets are managed through the web interface rather than YAML. It offers integrations with a long list of self-hosted services (such as Jellyfin, Sonarr, Home Assistant, Pi-hole, Proxmox and Uptime Kuma), with real-time widget updates via WebSockets, tRPC and Redis. It includes user management with permissions and groups, single sign-on via OIDC or LDAP, and a built-in search across integrated data. The README also mentions an icon picker with over 11K icons and encryption using BCrypt and AES-256-CBC. Kubernetes support with Helm is listed as well.
use_cases: monitor self-hosted services in one place
manage user access to a dashboard with groups
single sign-on for a home dashboard
how_to_run: See the official installation instructions linked from the README (the README itself does not list commands).
notable: Drag-and-drop grid layout configured through the web UI, no YAML needed
Large catalog of named integrations with self-hosted apps
OIDC and LDAP single sign-on with permissions and groups
Built-in search across integrated data and an icon picker with over 11K icons
Runs on x86, Raspberry Pi and Windows, Linux, TrueNAS, Unraid, per the README
caveats: Kubernetes and Helm support is described but setup details are not in the README
README points to external official installation instructions rather than giving steps inline
Sponsorship is requested to cover hosting and licensing costs, though the project is free to use
keywords: one page for all my services
